• Decorators: wrap functions/classes at definition
• Metaclasses: control class creation itself
• Often work together (e.g., @property is a descriptor)
20 Django ORM and metaclasses? Django, metaclass • ModelBase metaclass processes model fields
• Converts CharField() etc. into SQL schema
• Registers models in app registry
• Creates Meta inner class settings
21 abc.ABCMeta as metaclass? ABCMeta, abstract • ABCMeta tracks abstract methods on classes
• Prevents instantiation if abstracts remain
• class MyABC(metaclass=ABCMeta): or class MyABC(ABC):
• ABC is convenience class using ABCMeta
22 __prepare__ in metaclasses? prepare, namespace • __prepare__(mcs, name, bases) → returns namespace dict
• Called before class body executes
• Can return OrderedDict to track definition order
• Advanced — rarely needed
23 __init_subclass__ vs metaclass? init_subclass • __init_subclass__ — simple hook when subclassed (3.6+)
• Much simpler than metaclass
• Good for: registration, validation, adding methods
• Use metaclass only when you need full control
24 Metaclass vs class decorator vs __init_subclass__? Metaclass, choice • __init_subclass__ — simplest, handles most cases
• Class decorator — transforms class after creation
• Metaclass — full control over class creation
• Prefer: __init_subclass__ > class decorator > metaclass
25 __metaclass__ (Py2) vs metaclass= (Py3)? Python 2, metaclass • Python 2: __metaclass__ = Meta inside class body
• Python 3: class Foo(metaclass=Meta):
• Python 3 syntax is cleaner and explicit
• Python 2 is EOL — use Python 3

Section 7: Iterators & Generators¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Iterator protocol — __iter__ and __next__? Iterator, protocol • __iter__() → returns the iterator object itself
• __next__() → returns next value or raises StopIteration
• for loop calls both automatically
• Any object with these methods is an iterator
2 Iterable vs iterator? Iterable, iterator • Iterable: has __iter__() → can create iterator (list, str)
• Iterator: has __iter__() + __next__() → produces values
• Iterables reusable; iterators consumed once
• iter(iterable) → iterator
3 Custom iterator class? Custom, iterator • Class with __iter__ (return self) and __next__
• Track state in instance variables
• Raise StopIteration when done
• class Counter: def __next__(self): self.n += 1; return self.n
4 Generators — how does yield work? Generator, yield • yield pauses function, saves state, returns value
• Resumes on next next() call
• Function with yield → generator function
• Calling it returns generator object (not result)
5 Generator state between yield calls? Generator, state • All local variables preserved between yields
• Execution pointer saved at yield point
• Resumes exactly where it left off
• Stack frame kept alive until generator closes
6 Generator function vs generator expression? Generator, expression • Function: def gen(): yield 1; yield 2 (multi-statement)
• Expression: (x**2 for x in range(10)) (single expression)
• Both are lazy, same memory behavior
• Use expression for simple transformations
7 Generator expression vs list comprehension? Generator, list comp • Gen expr (x for x in …) → lazy, O(1) memory
• List comp [x for x in …] → eager, stores all in memory
• Use generator for large/infinite sequences
• Use list when need indexing or multiple passes
8 yield from? yield from, delegation • Delegates to a sub-iterator
• yield from another_generator() — forwards all values
• Cleaner than for x in gen(): yield x
• Also forwards .send() and .throw()
9 .send() to generator? send, generator • gen.send(value) → resumes and sends value into generator
• value = yield result — receives sent value
• First call must be next(gen) or gen.send(None)
• Enables coroutine-like behavior
10 .throw() and .close() on generators? throw, close • .throw(ExceptionType) → raises exception at yield point
• .close() → raises GeneratorExit to clean up
• .close() called automatically when generator is GC'd
• Used for cleanup in generator-based context managers
11 Generators save memory — example? Generator, memory • List of 1M ints: ~8MB; generator: ~120 bytes
• sum(x**2 for x in range(10**6)) → O(1) memory
• Reading large files: for line in open('huge.txt')
• Always prefer generators for large data
12 Chain multiple generators? Chain, generators • itertools.chain(gen1, gen2, gen3) — concatenate
• yield from gen1; yield from gen2 — manual
• All remain lazy
• Good for processing data pipelines
13 itertools — most useful functions? itertools, tools • chain — concatenate iterables
• islice — slice an iterator
• product — cartesian product
• combinations, permutations
• groupby, accumulate, zip_longest
14 chain, product, combinations, permutations? itertools, combinatorics • chain([1,2],[3,4]) → 1,2,3,4
• product('AB','12') → A1,A2,B1,B2
• combinations('ABC',2) → AB,AC,BC (no order)
• permutations('ABC',2) → AB,AC,BA,BC,CA,CB (order matters)
15 itertools.groupby — pitfall? groupby, sort • Groups consecutive elements with same key
• Must sort data first for full grouping
• groupby(sorted(data, key=fn), key=fn)
• Returns (key, group_iterator) pairs
16 itertools.islice? islice, slice • Slice an iterator (can't use [:] on iterators)
• islice(gen, 5) → first 5 elements
• islice(gen, 2, 8, 2) → start, stop, step
• Does not create a list in memory
17 Infinite generator (Fibonacci)? Infinite, Fibonacci • def fib(): a,b=0,1; while True: yield a; a,b=b,a+b
• Never terminates — use islice to limit
• list(islice(fib(), 10)) → first 10 Fibonacci
• Natural numbers: count(1) from itertools
18 Lazy evaluation and generators? Lazy, evaluation • Values computed on-demand (not upfront)
• Generators enable lazy evaluation in Python
• range() is lazy — doesn't create list
• File iteration is lazy — reads line by line
19 Generator to list — implications? List, materialize • list(gen) — materializes all values into memory
• Defeats purpose of lazy evaluation
• Generator is consumed (can't iterate again)
• Only materialize when needed
20 StopIteration? StopIteration, end • Signals end of iteration
• Raised by __next__() when exhausted
• for loop catches it automatically
• Don't raise it manually in generators (use return)
21 Reusable iterator? Reusable, iterator • Iterators are consumed once by default
• Solution: make __iter__ return NEW iterator each time
• Class with __iter__ returning fresh generator
• Iterable (not iterator) pattern
22 iter(callable, sentinel)? iter, sentinel • Two-argument form: calls callable until sentinel
• iter(input, 'quit') — reads until 'quit'
• iter(f.readline, '') — reads until empty line
• Useful for protocol-based reading
23 File line by line without loading all? File, lazy, line • for line in open('file.txt'): — iterator protocol
• File objects are iterators (lazy by default)
• with open('f') as f: for line in f: — best practice
• Don't use .readlines() for large files
24 Implement zip() from scratch? zip, generator • def my_zip(*iters): its = [iter(i) for i in iters]; while True: try: yield tuple(next(i) for i in its); except StopIteration: return
• Stops at shortest iterable
• Returns generator of tuples
25 Async generators? Async, generator • async def gen(): yield value — async generator
• async for x in gen(): — consume
• Use for streaming data, async I/O
• yield inside async def makes it async generator

Section 8: Exception Handling & Context Managers¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Syntax errors vs runtime exceptions? Syntax, runtime • Syntax error — detected before execution (parsing)
• Runtime exception — occurs during execution
• SyntaxError: invalid syntax vs ZeroDivisionError
• Fix syntax errors first; handle runtime with try/except
2 try/except/else/finally? try, except, finally • try → run risky code
• except Error as e → handle specific error
• else → runs if NO exception raised
• finally → ALWAYS runs (cleanup)
3 Why avoid bare except:? Bare except • Catches EVERYTHING including SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt
• Hides bugs — you can't see what went wrong
• Always catch specific exceptions
• At minimum: except Exception as e:
4 Multiple exception types in one except? Multiple, except • Tuple syntax: except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
• Each type gets same handler
• Or separate except blocks for different handling
• More specific exceptions first
5 Exception hierarchy? BaseException vs Exception? BaseException, hierarchy • BaseException → root of all exceptions
• Exception → inherits from BaseException (most errors)
• SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt → BaseException (not Exception)
• Always catch Exception, not BaseException
6 raise and exception chaining? raise, from • raise ValueError('msg') — throw exception
• raise alone — re-raises current exception
• raise New() from original — chains exceptions
• Chaining preserves original traceback
7 Custom exceptions? Custom, exception • class MyError(Exception): pass
• Add custom attributes in __init__
• Always inherit from Exception (not BaseException)
• Use for domain-specific error types
8 assert — when to use? assert, test • assert condition, 'message' — debug check
• Disabled with python -O (optimized mode)
• Never use for input validation or security
• Good for: invariants, dev-time checks
• Use exceptions for production validation
9 Exceptions in list comprehensions? Exception, comprehension • Can't use try/except inside comprehension directly
• Wrap in helper function: def safe(x): try: …except: return None
• [safe(x) for x in items]
• Or use generator with try/except
10 traceback module? traceback, inspect • traceback.print_exc() — print current exception
• traceback.format_exc() — get as string
• traceback.extract_tb(tb) — structured frames
• Used for logging exceptions
11 with statement — what problem? with, resource • Ensures cleanup even if exception occurs
• Replaces try/finally for resource management
• with open('f') as f: data = f.read() — auto-closes
• Works with any context manager
12 Context manager __enter__ / __exit__? enter, exit • __enter__ → setup, returns resource
• __exit__(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) → cleanup
• Return True from __exit__ to suppress exception
• Called automatically by with
13 @contextmanager decorator? contextmanager, yield • @contextlib.contextmanager
• def my_ctx(): setup(); try: yield resource; finally: cleanup()
• Simpler than class-based context manager
• yield is where with body runs
14 Class-based vs decorator-based context manager? Context, class vs deco • Class: more boilerplate, reusable, stateful
• Decorator: simpler, single-use-friendly
• Decorator: use for simple setup/teardown
• Class: use for complex state management
15 contextlib.suppress? suppress, ignore • with suppress(FileNotFoundError): os.remove('f')
• Silently ignores specified exception types
• Replaces try: …except: pass pattern
• Cleaner for expected, ignorable errors
16 contextlib.ExitStack? ExitStack, dynamic • Dynamically manage multiple context managers
• with ExitStack() as stack: files = [stack.enter_context(open(f)) for f in names]
• Variable number of contexts
• All cleaned up on exit
17 Exceptions in __exit__? exit, exception • __exit__ receives (exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb)
• All None if no exception
• Return True → suppress the exception
• Return False/None → exception propagates
18 Execution-time context manager? Timer, context • @contextmanager def timer(): start=time.time(); yield; print(f'{time.time()-start:.4f}s')
• with timer(): slow_operation()
• Setup before yield, cleanup after
19 Multiple context managers in one with? Multiple, with • with open('a') as f1, open('b') as f2:
• Python 3.10+: parenthesized form with (open('a') as f1, open('b') as f2):
• Or nested with blocks
20 contextlib.asynccontextmanager? Async, context • For async context managers
• @asynccontextmanager async def ctx(): yield resource
• async with ctx() as r:
• Used in async I/O (aiohttp, databases)
21 DB connection context manager? Database, context • __enter__ → connect, return connection
• __exit__ → commit on success, rollback on exception, close
• Ensures no leaked connections
• Most DB libraries provide this built-in
22 File lock context manager? Lock, context • __enter__ → acquire lock; __exit__ → release lock
• threading.Lock() is already a context manager
• with lock: critical_section()
• Ensures lock is always released
23 try/finally vs context manager? try, finally, with • Context manager = structured try/finally
• with is more readable and less error-prone
• Context manager is reusable across codebase
• Prefer with whenever possible
24 pathlib.Path.open() as context manager? pathlib, open • with Path('file.txt').open() as f: — auto-closes
• Path('f').read_text() — shortcut (no with needed)
• Path('f').write_text('content') — write shortcut
• pathlib preferred over os.path
25 ExceptionGroup and except* (3.11+)? ExceptionGroup, except* • Group multiple exceptions: ExceptionGroup('msg', [e1, e2])
• except* ValueError as eg: — catches ValueError subgroup
• For concurrent tasks with multiple failures
• Used with asyncio.TaskGroup

Section 9: File I/O & Serialization¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 File opening modes? open, modes • 'r' read (default), 'w' write (overwrites)
• 'a' append, 'x' exclusive create
• 'b' binary, 't' text (default)
• 'rb' read binary, 'r+' read+write
• Always specify encoding='utf-8'
2 read() vs readline() vs readlines()? read, readline • read() → entire file as one string
• read(n) → first n characters
• readline() → single line (with \n)
• readlines() → list of all lines
• Best: iterate file object directly
3 write() vs writelines()? write, writelines • write(str) → writes string, returns char count
• writelines(list) → writes list of strings (no newlines added)
• Neither adds \n automatically
• Use print(line, file=f) for auto-newline
4 Why with open() over manual open/close? with, open, close • Guarantees file is closed even on exception
• No need for explicit f.close()
• Prevents resource leaks
• Pythonic best practice
5 Read large file line by line? Large file, lazy • with open('f') as f: for line in f: — lazy iteration
• File object is an iterator (one line at a time)
• Never use .readlines() for large files
• Also: for line in fileinput.input()
6 File encoding issues? Default encoding? Encoding, utf-8 • Default varies by OS (Windows: 'cp1252', Unix: 'utf-8')
• Always specify: open('f', encoding='utf-8')
• Python 3.15: UTF-8 becomes universal default
• errors='replace' for graceful handling
7 seek() and tell()? seek, tell, random • tell() → current position in file
• seek(offset, whence) → move to position
• seek(0) → go to beginning
• seek(0, 2) → go to end
8 Text mode vs binary mode? Text, binary • Text: strings, with encoding/decoding, newline conversion
• Binary: bytes, no encoding, exact data
• 'rb'/'wb' for images, audio, etc.
• Binary for network protocols, struct packing
9 CSV with csv module? csv, reader, writer • csv.reader(f) → iterate rows as lists
• csv.writer(f).writerow([…])
• csv.DictReader(f) → rows as dicts (header keys)
• csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=[…])
10 json.dump/load vs json.dumps/loads? json, dump, dumps • dump(obj, file) / load(file) → file operations
• dumps(obj) / loads(str) → string operations
• 's' suffix = string; no 's' = file
• Common: json.dump(data, open('f','w'), indent=2)
11 Non-serializable objects in JSON? JSON, datetime • Default: only dict, list, str, int, float, bool, None
• Custom: json.dumps(obj, default=str) — convert all to str
• Better: default=lambda o: o.isoformat() for datetime
• Or subclass JSONEncoder
12 pickle vs JSON? Security risks? pickle, JSON • Pickle: Python-specific binary format, any object
• JSON: text, cross-language, limited types
• Never unpickle untrusted data — code execution risk
• JSON for APIs/config; pickle for internal caching
13 shelve module? shelve, persistence • Dict-like persistent storage using pickle
• with shelve.open('db') as db: db['key'] = value
• Simple key-value store backed by file
• Same security risks as pickle
14 YAML files in Python? YAML, PyYAML • pip install pyyaml
• yaml.safe_load(f) → dict (SAFE — no code exec)
• yaml.dump(data, f) → write YAML
• Never use yaml.load() without Loader
15 Check if file/directory exists? exists, path • Path('f').exists() — file or dir
• Path('f').is_file() — specifically file
• Path('f').is_dir() — specifically directory
• os.path.exists('f') — older style
16 os.path vs pathlib? os.path, pathlib • pathlib (preferred): OOP, readable, chainable
• Path('dir') / 'sub' / 'f.txt' vs os.path.join(…)
• path.read_text(), .glob(), .stem, .suffix
• pathlib since Python 3.4
17 List files recursively? Recursive, glob • Path('dir').rglob('*.py') — recursive glob
• os.walk('dir') → (dirpath, dirnames, filenames)
• glob.glob('**/*.py', recursive=True)
• pathlib rglob is most readable
18 Read/write binary files? Binary, images • with open('img.png', 'rb') as f: data = f.read()
• with open('out.png', 'wb') as f: f.write(data)
• Use struct for packed binary data
• Use dedicated libraries for specific formats
19 tempfile module? tempfile, temporary • tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() — auto-deleted
• tempfile.mkdtemp() — temporary directory
• tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile() — in-memory until size limit
• Safe for sensitive data (random names)
20 shutil for file operations? shutil, copy, move • shutil.copy(src, dst) — copy file
• shutil.copytree(src, dst) — copy directory
• shutil.move(src, dst) — move/rename
• shutil.make_archive() — zip/tar
21 io.StringIO and io.BytesIO? StringIO, BytesIO • In-memory file-like objects
• StringIO() for text, BytesIO() for bytes
• Useful for testing, API adapters
• s = StringIO(); s.write('hello'); s.getvalue()
22 Memory-mapped files (mmap)? mmap, memory • Map file into memory for fast random access
• with mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0) as mm: mm[0:5]
• Efficient for large files with random reads
• OS handles paging transparently
23 Concurrent file writes? Concurrent, write • Use file locking: fcntl.flock() on Unix
• Or threading.Lock() for same-process threads
• Append mode is mostly atomic for small writes
• Better: use database for concurrent access
24 stdin/stdout for CLI tools? stdin, stdout • sys.stdin.readline() or input()
• sys.stdout.write(str) or print()
• sys.stdin is iterable: for line in sys.stdin:
• Redirect: python script.py < input.txt > output.txt
25 File-based key-value store? Key-value, file • shelve — built-in solution
• JSON file: load, modify, write back
• sqlite3 — better for concurrent access
• dbm — low-level dict-like file

Section 10: Modules, Packages & Imports¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Module vs package? Module, package • Module: single .py file
• Package: directory with __init__.py (or namespace package)
• Package can contain modules and sub-packages
• Both importable with import
2 Import system internally? Import, system • Checks sys.modules cache first
• Searches sys.path for module
• Compiles to bytecode (.pyc)
• Executes module code on first import
• Subsequent imports use cache
3 sys.path import resolution? sys.path, resolve • List of directories Python searches for modules
• Order: script dir → PYTHONPATH → site-packages
• sys.path.insert(0, '/my/path') to add
• .pth files in site-packages auto-add paths
4 __init__.py — required in Python 3? init, package • Not required (namespace packages exist since 3.3)
• But recommended for regular packages
• Used to initialize package, define __all__
• Can be empty or contain package-level code
5 if __name__ == '__main__'? name, main • __name__ = '__main__' when run directly
• __name__ = module name when imported
• Guards code from running on import
• Essential for reusable scripts
6 Absolute vs relative imports? Absolute, relative • Absolute: from mypackage.utils import func
• Relative: from .utils import func (same package)
• .. goes up one level: from ..core import Base
• Relative only inside packages
7 Circular imports — how to fix? Circular, import • A imports B, B imports A → ImportError
• Fix 1: move import inside function (lazy)
• Fix 2: restructure to avoid circular dependency
• Fix 3: combine into single module
8 __all__? all, star import • __all__ = ['func1', 'Class1']
• Controls what from module import * exports
• Doesn't affect direct imports
• Best practice: always define in public modules
9 Reload module at runtime? Reload, importlib • importlib.reload(module) — re-executes module
• Module must already be imported
• Doesn't update existing references
• Rarely needed — mostly for development
10 Dynamic imports with importlib? importlib, dynamic • importlib.import_module('module.name')
• importlib.import_module('.sub', 'package')
• Returns module object
• Used for plugin systems
11 Namespace package? Namespace, PEP 420 • Package without __init__.py (PEP 420)
• Can span multiple directories
• Portions auto-discovered across sys.path
• Used by large frameworks with split installations
12 __main__.py? main, executable • Makes package runnable: python -m mypackage
• Equivalent to if __name__ == '__main__' for packages
• Contains entry point code
• Common in CLI tools
13 Python project structure? Structure, project • src/mypackage/ layout (recommended)
• tests/, docs/, pyproject.toml
• __init__.py in each sub-package
• src layout prevents import confusion
14 Script vs module? Script, module • Script: executed directly (python script.py)
• Module: imported by other code
• Same file can be both (with __main__ guard)
• Scripts have __name__ == '__main__'
15 Handle import errors gracefully? ImportError, optional • try: import optional_lib; except ImportError: optional_lib = None
• Check before use: if optional_lib:
• Common for optional dependencies
• Also: ModuleNotFoundError (Python 3.6+)
16 sys.modules cache? sys.modules, cache • Dict of all imported modules
• Import checks here first (O(1))
• Can be manipulated: del sys.modules['name']
• Used for lazy loading and testing
17 Plugin system with dynamic imports? Plugin, dynamic • Discover plugin files: glob('plugins/*.py')
• Import: importlib.import_module(name)
• Register via __init_subclass__ or metaclass
• Entry points: importlib.metadata.entry_points()
18 pip install -e . (editable) vs regular? Editable, develop • Regular: copies package to site-packages
• Editable (-e): symlinks, changes reflect immediately
• Used during development
• pip install -e . or pip install -e '.[dev]'
19 pyproject.toml vs setup.py? pyproject, setup • pyproject.toml — modern standard (PEP 518/621)
• setup.py — legacy, still supported
• setup.cfg — declarative config (semi-legacy)
• New projects should use pyproject.toml
20 Virtual environments — venv vs virtualenv? venv, virtualenv • venv — built-in, lighter, recommended
• virtualenv — third-party, more features
• python -m venv .venv → create
• source .venv/bin/activate → activate
• Isolates project dependencies

Section 11: Memory Management & Garbage Collection¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 How does Python manage memory? Memory, allocation • Private heap managed by Python memory manager
• Object-specific allocators (int, list, dict)
• pymalloc for small objects (≤512 bytes)
• Large objects use system malloc
2 Reference counting in CPython? Refcount, CPython • Each object has a reference count
• Incremented on assignment, parameter passing
• Decremented when variable deleted or goes out of scope
• Object freed when count reaches 0
3 Garbage collector (gc module)? gc, garbage • Supplements reference counting
• Detects and collects circular references
• Runs automatically at thresholds
• gc.collect() to force collection
• gc.disable() / gc.enable()
4 Circular references? Circular, cycle • Object A refs B, B refs A → refcount never reaches 0
• Reference counting alone can't handle this
• Cyclic GC detects and breaks these cycles
• Common with parent-child relationships
5 del vs garbage collection? del, gc • del x — removes NAME binding, decrements refcount
• Does NOT necessarily free memory
• Object freed only when refcount = 0 AND no cycles
• GC handles cycles separately
6 Force garbage collection? gc.collect, force • gc.collect() — runs full collection
• Returns number of unreachable objects found
• Useful after deleting large data structures
• Usually not needed — GC runs automatically
7 sys.getrefcount() — why one higher? getrefcount, ref • Returns reference count of object
• Always seems +1 because getrefcount itself holds a reference
• sys.getrefcount(x) → actual refs + 1
• Useful for debugging memory issues
8 Generations in GC? Generations, gc • 3 generations: gen 0 (new), gen 1, gen 2 (old)
• New objects start in gen 0
• Surviving objects promoted to next gen
• Gen 0 collected most frequently
• Generational hypothesis: most objects die young
9 sys.getsizeof() limitations? getsizeof, size • Returns size of ONE object (bytes)
• Does NOT include referenced objects
• getsizeof([1,2,3]) — only list overhead, not ints
• For total: use pympler.asizeof or traverse manually
10 __del__ — why unreliable? del, destructor • Called when refcount reaches 0 (not guaranteed when)
• Not called for circular references (may never run)
• Don't rely on it for cleanup — use context managers
• Can prevent GC of circular references
11 Weak references (weakref)? weakref, reference • Reference that doesn't increment refcount
• ref = weakref.ref(obj) — access via ref()
• Returns None when object is collected
• Used in caches, observer patterns to avoid leaks
12 Python memory pool allocator (pymalloc)? pymalloc, allocator • Specialized allocator for objects ≤512 bytes
• Manages pools of fixed-size blocks
• Reduces overhead of calling malloc repeatedly
• Arenas (256KB) → pools → blocks
13 Detecting memory leaks? Memory leak, detect • tracemalloc — built-in, tracks allocations
• objgraph — visualize reference graphs
• gc.get_referrers(obj) — who references this?
• Look for: growing collections, circular refs, caches
14 Memory profiling tools? tracemalloc, profiler • tracemalloc.start() → .take_snapshot() → compare
• memory_profiler — line-by-line: @profile
• objgraph — reference counting visualization
• pympler — detailed object tracking
15 Object interning? Interning, cache • Python caches frequently used immutable objects
• Small integers (-5 to 256) always interned
• Short strings (identifier-like) often interned
• sys.intern('string') — force interning
16 Small integer cache (-5 to 256)? Integer cache, 256 • CPython pre-creates ints -5 to 256 at startup
• a = 256; b = 256; a is b → True (same object)
• a = 257; b = 257; a is b → False (different objects)
• Implementation detail — don't rely on it
17 CPython vs PyPy memory management? CPython, PyPy • CPython: refcounting + cyclic GC
• PyPy: tracing GC (no refcounting)
• PyPy uses less memory for many objects
• PyPy's GC has better throughput, worse latency
18 __slots__ and memory? slots, memory • Replaces per-instance __dict__ with fixed slots
• Saves 40-50% memory per instance
• __slots__ = ('x', 'y')
• Most impactful with millions of instances
19 Profiling and reducing memory in data apps? Memory, data • Use generators instead of lists
• Process data in chunks (pandas chunksize)
• Use appropriate dtypes (int32 vs int64)
• Dereference large objects early (del df)
20 Generators vs lists — memory? Generator, memory • List: stores ALL elements in memory
• Generator: computes one at a time (O(1) memory)
• sum(x**2 for x in range(10**6)) — O(1) memory
• [x**2 for x in range(10**6)] — O(n) memory

Section 12: Concurrency & Parallelism¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is the GIL? Why does it exist? GIL, CPython • Global Interpreter Lock in CPython
• Only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time
• Exists to protect CPython's reference counting
• Simplifies C extension development
2 GIL and multi-threaded programs? GIL, threads • CPU-bound threads don't run in parallel
• I/O-bound threads DO benefit (GIL released during I/O)
• Multi-threaded CPU work → use multiprocessing
• Python 3.13+ has experimental no-GIL mode
3 Concurrency vs parallelism? Concurrency, parallelism • Concurrency: tasks make progress (interleaving)
• Parallelism: tasks run simultaneously (multi-core)
• Threading = concurrency (GIL limits parallelism)
• Multiprocessing = true parallelism
4 Threading vs multiprocessing vs asyncio? Threading, multiprocessing • Threading: I/O-bound, shared memory, GIL limited
• Multiprocessing: CPU-bound, separate memory, true parallel
• asyncio: I/O-bound, single-threaded, cooperative
• Choose based on workload type
5 threading module — create threads? threading, Thread • t = threading.Thread(target=func, args=(x,))
• t.start() → run; t.join() → wait
• t.daemon = True → dies with main thread
• Or subclass Thread and override run()
6 Thread limitations for CPU-bound? Thread, CPU, GIL • GIL prevents true parallel execution
• CPU-bound threads → slower than single-threaded
• Thread switching adds overhead
• Solution: multiprocessing or ProcessPoolExecutor
7 When are threads useful despite GIL? Thread, I/O • I/O-bound tasks: network, file, database
• GIL released during I/O operations
• Multiple network requests in parallel
• GUI responsiveness (background work)
8 Race condition — prevention? Race condition, lock • Multiple threads access shared data simultaneously
• Results depend on timing (non-deterministic)
• Fix: threading.Lock() — mutual exclusion
• with lock: shared_data += 1
9 threading.Lock? Lock, mutex • lock = threading.Lock()
• lock.acquire() / lock.release()
• Better: with lock: (auto-release)
• Only one thread holds lock at a time
10 Lock vs RLock? Lock, RLock, reentrant • Lock — can't be acquired twice by same thread (deadlock)
• RLock — reentrant, same thread can acquire multiple times
• RLock tracks acquire count, must release same times
• Use RLock for recursive/nested locking
11 Deadlock — prevention? Deadlock, prevention • Two threads each hold a lock the other needs
• Prevention: always acquire locks in same order
• Use timeout: lock.acquire(timeout=5)
• Avoid nested locks when possible
12 Semaphore? Semaphore, limit • Like Lock but allows N concurrent accesses
• sem = Semaphore(3) → max 3 threads
• Used for connection pools, rate limiting
• BoundedSemaphore — error if released too many times
13 threading.Event? Event, signal • Flag for thread communication
• event.set() → signal; event.wait() → block until set
• event.clear() → reset; event.is_set() → check
• One-shot or repeated signaling
14 threading.Condition? Condition, wait • Combines Lock + wait/notify
• cond.wait() — release lock, wait for notify
• cond.notify() — wake one waiter; notify_all()
• Producer-consumer pattern
15 queue.Queue — thread-safe? Queue, thread-safe • Built-in thread-safe FIFO queue
• q.put(item) / q.get() — block if full/empty
• q.task_done() / q.join() — track completion
• No external locking needed
16 multiprocessing — bypassing GIL? multiprocessing, GIL • Each process has its own GIL (separate interpreter)
• True parallel execution on multiple cores
• Process(target=func) — similar API to threading
• Higher overhead (process creation, IPC)
17 Sharing data between processes? IPC, Queue, Pipe • multiprocessing.Queue — process-safe queue
• Pipe() — two-way connection
• Value('i', 0), Array('d', [1,2,3]) — shared memory
• Manager() — shared dicts, lists
18 concurrent.futures — ThreadPool/ProcessPool? concurrent.futures, pool • ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) — thread pool
• ProcessPoolExecutor() — process pool
• Same API, swap implementations easily
• Higher-level than raw threading/multiprocessing
19 executor.map() vs executor.submit()? map, submit, future • map(fn, items) → ordered results, blocks until done
• submit(fn, arg) → returns Future, non-blocking
• future.result() to get result
• as_completed(futures) — process as they finish
20 asyncio — async/await? asyncio, async, await • async def defines coroutine function
• await pauses until operation completes
• asyncio.run(main()) starts event loop
• Single-threaded, cooperative concurrency
21 Event loop — how asyncio works? Event loop, asyncio • Central loop managing all async operations
• Runs coroutines, handles I/O events
• Tasks yield control at await points
• One task runs at a time (no GIL issues)
22 Coroutines vs generators? Coroutine, generator • Generators produce values (yield)
• Coroutines consume AND produce (await)
• Coroutines are for async I/O
• async def creates native coroutine (not generator)
23 gather() vs wait() vs create_task()? gather, wait, task • create_task(coro) → schedules coroutine as Task
• gather(*coros) → run concurrently, return all results
• wait(tasks) → more control (done/pending sets)
• TaskGroup (3.11+) — structured concurrency
24 Exceptions in async code? Async, exception • try/except works normally in async functions
• gather(return_exceptions=True) → collect errors
• Unhandled in tasks → logged as warnings
• TaskGroup cancels siblings on exception
25 aiohttp vs requests? aiohttp, requests • requests — synchronous, blocking
• aiohttp — async, non-blocking
• httpx — supports both sync + async
• Use async for many concurrent requests
26 asyncio.Semaphore — rate limiting? Semaphore, rate limit • sem = asyncio.Semaphore(10) — max 10 concurrent
• async with sem: await request()
• Prevents overwhelming external APIs
• Essential for well-behaved scrapers
27 CPU-bound vs I/O-bound — choosing model? CPU, I/O, choice • I/O-bound: asyncio (best) or threading
• CPU-bound: multiprocessing
• Mixed: combine (asyncio + ProcessPoolExecutor)
• Profile first to determine bottleneck
28 Blocking code in async (run_in_executor)? Executor, async • await loop.run_in_executor(None, blocking_fn)
• Runs blocking code in thread pool
• Prevents blocking the event loop
• asyncio.to_thread(fn) (3.9+) — simpler
29 Async context managers and iterators? Async, context, iter • async with → __aenter__ / __aexit__
• async for → __aiter__ / __anext__
• Used for async DB connections, streaming
• @asynccontextmanager decorator
30 Testing async code? Async, test, pytest • pytest-asyncio — @pytest.mark.asyncio
• asyncio.run(coro) in tests
• Mock async functions with AsyncMock
• aioresponses for mocking HTTP

Section 13: Advanced Python Concepts¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Descriptors powering @property, @classmethod, @staticmethod? Descriptor, protocol • Descriptors define __get__, __set__, __delete__
• property is a data descriptor (has __set__)
• classmethod.__get__ binds cls as first arg
• staticmethod.__get__ returns raw function
2 __getattr__ vs __getattribute__? getattr, getattribute • __getattribute__ — called on EVERY attribute access
• __getattr__ — called only when attribute NOT found
• Override __getattr__ for fallback behavior
• Override __getattribute__ carefully (easy infinite recursion)
3 __setattr__ — infinite recursion? setattr, recursion • Called on every self.x = val
• Inside __setattr__, self.x = val calls itself recursively
• Fix: object.__setattr__(self, 'x', val)
• Or use self.__dict__['x'] = val
4 typing.Protocol (3.8+)? Protocol, structural • Structural subtyping — no explicit inheritance needed
• class Drawable(Protocol): def draw(self): ...
• Any class with draw() satisfies Drawable
• Checked by mypy, not at runtime (by default)
5 Structural vs nominal subtyping? Structural, nominal • Nominal: explicit class Dog(Animal) — must inherit
• Structural: just implement the interface (duck typing)
• Python traditionally uses structural (duck typing)
• Protocol formalizes structural subtyping
6 TypeVar, Generic — generic code? TypeVar, Generic • T = TypeVar('T') — type placeholder
• class Stack(Generic[T]): def push(self, item: T)
• def first(items: list[T]) -> T: — generic func
• Enables type-safe reusable components
7 TypedDict and Literal types? TypedDict, Literal • TypedDict('User', name=str, age=int) — typed dict
• Literal['read', 'write'] — exact value types
• Both for static type checking only
• No runtime enforcement
8 dataclasses.field() customization? field, dataclass • field(default_factory=list) — mutable defaults
• field(repr=False) — exclude from repr
• field(compare=False) — exclude from equality
• field(init=False) — exclude from __init__
9 __post_init__ in dataclasses? post_init, init • Called after auto-generated __init__
• Used for validation, derived fields
• Access all init fields via self
• InitVar[type] for init-only params
10 Enums — IntEnum, Flag, auto()? Enum, IntEnum • class Color(Enum): RED = 1 — standard enum
• IntEnum — can be compared with ints
• Flag — supports bitwise operations
• auto() — auto-assign values
11 __class_getitem__ — MyClass[int] syntax? class_getitem • Enables subscript syntax: Stack[int]
• def __class_getitem__(cls, item): — returns parameterized type
• Used by list[int], dict[str, int] internally
• Custom generics implement this
12 abc module — abstract base classes? abc, abstract • from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
• class Shape(ABC): @abstractmethod def area(self):
• Can't instantiate ABC directly
• Subclass MUST implement all abstract methods
13 __subclasshook__? subclasshook • Override isinstance/issubclass checks
• Used by ABCs to accept structural subtypes
• If returns True → class is considered subclass
• NotImplemented → fall back to normal check
14 Custom pickling with __reduce__? reduce, pickle • __reduce__ returns (constructor, args) tuple
• Controls how object is pickled/unpickled
• Needed for objects with non-picklable state
• copyreg.pickle(type, reduce_func)
15 __format__ method? format, format • Called by format() and f-strings
• def __format__(self, spec): return ...
• Controls custom format specs: f"{obj:.2f}"
• format(obj, '.2f') calls obj.__format__('.2f')
16 Context variables (contextvars)? contextvars, context • Task-local storage (3.7+)
• var = ContextVar('name', default=val)
• Each asyncio task gets its own context
• Unlike thread-local: works with async tasks
17 sys.settrace() and sys.setprofile()? settrace, setprofile • settrace(fn) → called for every line/call/return
• Used by debuggers (pdb) and coverage tools
• setprofile(fn) → called on call/return only
• Significant performance overhead
18 Attribute lookup chain? Lookup, MRO • Instance __dict__ → class __dict__ → base classes (MRO)
• Data descriptors override instance dict
• Non-data descriptors lose to instance dict
• __getattr__ is last resort fallback
19 Cooperative __init__ in multiple inheritance? Cooperative, super • Each __init__ calls super().__init__()
• MRO determines order
• All __init__s in chain get called
• Use **kwargs to pass through extra args
20 __missing__ in dict subclasses? missing, dict • Called when key not found in __getitem__
• defaultdict uses this internally
• def __missing__(self, key): self[key] = default; return default
• Only affects d[key], not d.get(key)
21 __contains__ vs __getitem__ for in? contains, in • in checks __contains__ first
• If no __contains__, falls back to __getitem__ iteration
• __contains__ is O(1) for sets/dicts
• __getitem__ fallback is O(n)
22 Immutable data structures? Immutable, frozen • tuple, frozenset, str — built-in immutable
• @dataclass(frozen=True) — frozen dataclass
• NamedTuple — immutable by default
• Override __setattr__ to raise TypeError
23 __sizeof__ vs sys.getsizeof()? sizeof, getsizeof • __sizeof__ → memory of object itself
• sys.getsizeof() → __sizeof__ + GC overhead
• Neither includes referenced objects
• Use pympler.asizeof for deep size
24 Observer pattern with __set_name__ and descriptors? set_name, observer • __set_name__(self, owner, name) — called when descriptor assigned to class
• Descriptor knows its attribute name automatically
• Can register watchers in __set__
• Clean pattern for reactive attributes
25 Late binding in closures — bug and fix? Late binding, closure • fns = [lambda: i for i in range(3)] — all return 2!
• i is looked up at call time, not definition time
• Fix: default arg lambda i=i: i
• Or functools.partial(fn, i)

Section 14: Standard Library Deep Dive¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Most important stdlib modules? stdlib, modules • os, sys, pathlib — filesystem/system
• collections, itertools, functools — data/functions
• json, csv, re — parsing
• datetime, logging, subprocess — utilities
• typing, dataclasses, enum — modern Python
2 collections.Counter — useful methods? Counter, methods • Counter('banana') → {'a':3,'n':2,'b':1}
• .most_common(n) — top N elements
• .elements() → iterator of all elements
• Arithmetic: c1 + c2, c1 - c2, c1 & c2, union
3 defaultdict with lambda factory? defaultdict, lambda • defaultdict(lambda: 'unknown') — custom default
• defaultdict(lambda: []) — same as defaultdict(list)
• Lambda needed for non-callable defaults
• Factory called each time (new instance)
4 heapq — N largest/smallest? heapq, nlargest • heapq.nlargest(k, items) — top k elements
• heapq.nsmallest(k, items) — bottom k
• key= parameter for custom comparison
• For k=1: use max()/min() instead
5 bisect — maintaining sorted list? bisect, sorted • bisect_left(a, x) → insertion point (left of equal)
• insort(a, x) → insert maintaining sort
• O(log n) search, O(n) insert
• Used for ordered data, ranking
6 lru_cache internals? lru_cache, internal • Doubly-linked list + dict for O(1) operations
• Dict: key → linked list node
• Access moves node to front
• Evicts from back when full
7 functools.total_ordering? total_ordering • Define __eq__ + one comparison (__lt__)
• Generates __le__, __gt__, __ge__ automatically
• Slight performance overhead (derived methods)
• Convenient for sortable classes
8 datetime, timedelta, timezone? datetime, timedelta • datetime.now() — current date/time
• timedelta(days=7) — duration, arithmetic
• datetime.now(timezone.utc) — timezone-aware
• strftime('%Y-%m-%d') for formatting
9 datetime.now() vs datetime.utcnow() issue? utcnow, timezone • utcnow() returns naive UTC datetime
• Missing timezone info → causes bugs
• Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) instead
• utcnow() deprecated in Python 3.12
10 logging module — levels? logging, levels • DEBUG < INFO < WARNING < ERROR < CRITICAL
• logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
• logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
• Never use print() for production logging
11 Logging handlers and formatters? Logging, handler • StreamHandler → console; FileHandler → file
• RotatingFileHandler → auto-rotate by size
• Formatter('%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s')
• Configure via dictConfig() or fileConfig()
12 argparse — CLI tools? argparse, CLI • parser = ArgumentParser(description='…')
• parser.add_argument('file', help='…') — positional
• parser.add_argument('-v', '--verbose', action='store_true')
• args = parser.parse_args() → namespace
13 subprocess vs os.system()? subprocess, os.system • os.system() — legacy, no output capture
• subprocess.run(['cmd', 'arg']) — modern, flexible
• capture_output=True → get stdout/stderr
• check=True → raise on non-zero exit
14 subprocess.run() vs Popen()? run, Popen • run() — simple, waits for completion
• Popen() — low-level, non-blocking, streaming
• run() sufficient for most cases
• Popen() for concurrent I/O, pipes between processes
15 re module — common patterns? re, regex • \d+ digits, \w+ word chars, \s+ whitespace
• ^$ anchors, . any char, *+? quantifiers
• ( ) capture groups, (?:) non-capturing
• re.IGNORECASE, re.MULTILINE flags
16 dataclasses.asdict() and astuple()? asdict, astuple • asdict(instance) → recursive dict conversion
• astuple(instance) → recursive tuple conversion
• Handles nested dataclasses
• Useful for JSON serialization
17 enum.auto() — custom enum values? enum, auto • class Color(Enum): RED = auto(); BLUE = auto()
• auto() assigns incrementing integers
• Override _generate_next_value_ for custom logic
• StrEnum (3.11+): auto uses lowercase name
18 Protocol vs ABC — when to choose? Protocol, ABC • Protocol → structural subtyping, no inheritance needed
• ABC → nominal subtyping, must inherit explicitly
• Protocol better for third-party code you can't modify
• ABC better for enforcing implementation contracts
19 secrets vs random for security? secrets, random • random — NOT cryptographically secure (predictable)
• secrets — secure random for tokens, passwords
• secrets.token_hex(32), secrets.token_urlsafe()
• Never use random for security
20 hashlib — SHA-256, MD5? hashlib, hash • hashlib.sha256(b'data').hexdigest()
• hashlib.md5(b'data').hexdigest() — not for security
• Use SHA-256 for integrity, bcrypt for passwords
• hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac() for key derivation
21 struct module — binary packing? struct, binary • struct.pack('!HI', 8080, 12345) → bytes
• struct.unpack('!HI', data) → tuple
• Format: H=uint16, I=uint32, !=network byte order
• Used for binary protocols, file formats
22 abc.abstractmethod — abstract properties? abstractmethod, property • @property @abstractmethod def name(self): — abstract property
• Both decorators needed (order matters in 3.3+)
• Subclass must implement as property
• Can also have abstract classmethods/staticmethods
23 warnings module — deprecation? warnings, deprecation • warnings.warn('msg', DeprecationWarning)
• warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=…)
• warnings.simplefilter('error') — turn warnings into errors
• Use for gentle migration paths
24 Decimal vs float? When use Decimal? Decimal, float • float: fast but imprecise (0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3)
• Decimal: exact decimal arithmetic
• Use Decimal for: money, financial calculations
• Decimal('0.1') + Decimal('0.2') == Decimal('0.3')
25 fractions.Fraction? Fraction, rational • Exact rational arithmetic: Fraction(1, 3) → 1/3
• Fraction('0.1') — exact
• Arithmetic preserves exact values
• Use when exact fractions matter

Section 15: Testing & Debugging¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Unit testing — why important? Unit test, importance • Catches bugs early (before production)
• Documents expected behavior
• Enables safe refactoring
• Fast feedback loop
• Required for CI/CD
2 unittest vs pytest? unittest, pytest • pytest: simpler, assert based, better output
• unittest: class-based, built-in, verbose
• pytest: fixtures, parametrize, plugins
• Industry standard: pytest
3 Basic pytest test? pytest, basic • def test_add(): assert add(2, 3) == 5
• File: test_*.py or *_test.py
• Run: pytest or pytest -v
• No class needed — just functions
4 pytest fixtures and scopes? Fixture, scope • @pytest.fixture def db(): return connect(); yield; close()
• Scopes: function (default), class, module, session
• session scope: created once for all tests
• Fixtures inject dependencies
5 @pytest.mark.parametrize? Parametrize, test • @pytest.mark.parametrize('x,y,expected', [(1,2,3),(0,0,0)])
• Runs test once per parameter set
• Avoids duplicating test functions
• Clear failure messages per case
6 Test expected exceptions in pytest? Exception, pytest • with pytest.raises(ValueError): dangerous_func()
• with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='msg'):
• Can inspect: excinfo.value, excinfo.type
• Tests that exceptions ARE raised
7 Mocking — when to mock? Mock, when • Mock external dependencies (APIs, databases, files)
• Don't mock the code under test
• Don't mock simple, fast, deterministic code
• Mock at the boundary (I/O, network, time)
8 unittest.mock.patch and MagicMock? patch, MagicMock • @patch('module.Class.method') — replaces with mock
• MagicMock — auto-creates attributes/return values
• mock.return_value = 42
• mock.assert_called_once_with(args)
9 Mock vs MagicMock? Mock, MagicMock • MagicMock extends Mock with magic methods
• MagicMock has __len__, __iter__, etc. pre-configured
• Use MagicMock by default
• Use Mock when you explicitly want no magic
10 side_effect in mocking? side_effect, mock • mock.side_effect = Exception('boom') — raises on call
• mock.side_effect = [1, 2, 3] — returns sequentially
• mock.side_effect = lambda x: x * 2 — custom logic
• Overrides return_value
11 Mock external API calls? API, mock, patch • @patch('requests.get') at the test
• mock_get.return_value.json.return_value = {...}
• Or use responses library for more control
• Mock at the boundary, not deep inside code
12 Test coverage with coverage.py? Coverage, pytest-cov • pytest --cov=mypackage --cov-report=html
• Shows which lines were executed
• Aim for 80%+ but don't obsess over 100%
• Coverage ≠ correctness
13 TDD — pros and cons? TDD, test-driven • Write test → fail → implement → pass → refactor
• Pros: better design, fewer bugs, documentation
• Cons: slower initial development, can feel rigid
• Works well for complex business logic
14 Tests for async functions? Async, test • pytest-asyncio: @pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_x()
• AsyncMock for mocking async functions
• asyncio.run() for simple cases
• aioresponses for HTTP mocking
15 Test doubles: stub, mock, fake, spy, dummy? Test doubles, types • Dummy: passed but never used
• Stub: returns predefined values
• Spy: records calls, delegates to real
• Mock: verifies interactions/expectations
• Fake: working but simplified implementation
16 Structure tests in large project? Test, structure • Mirror source structure: tests/test_module.py
• conftest.py for shared fixtures
• Separate: unit, integration, e2e
• pytest.ini or pyproject.toml for config
17 conftest.py in pytest? conftest, pytest • Shared fixtures/hooks available to all tests in directory
• Auto-discovered by pytest (no import needed)
• Can have multiple at different levels
• Used for: DB connections, test data, plugins
18 pytest markers? Markers, pytest • @pytest.mark.slow — custom category
• pytest -m 'not slow' — skip slow tests
• @pytest.mark.skip(reason='…') — skip
• @pytest.mark.xfail — expected failure
19 pdb — breakpoints? pdb, debugger • import pdb; pdb.set_trace() — pause here
• breakpoint() — Python 3.7+ (same thing)
• Commands: n next, s step, c continue, p print
• l list code, q quit
20 breakpoint() function (3.7+)? breakpoint, debug • Built-in, replaces pdb.set_trace()
• Respects PYTHONBREAKPOINT env var
• PYTHONBREAKPOINT=0 — disable all breakpoints
• PYTHONBREAKPOINT=ipdb.set_trace — use ipdb
21 cProfile and timeit? cProfile, timeit • cProfile.run('func()') — function-level profiling
• python -m cProfile script.py — CLI
• timeit.timeit('expr', number=10000) — micro-benchmarks
• %%timeit in Jupyter
22 Debug memory issues? Memory, debug • tracemalloc.start() → track allocations
• objgraph.show_most_common_types()
• gc.get_referrers(obj) — who holds references?
• memory_profiler for line-by-line
23 Integration vs unit vs e2e tests? Integration, e2e • Unit: single function/class, fast, isolated
• Integration: multiple components working together
• E2E: full system from user perspective
• Pyramid: many unit > some integration > few e2e
24 doctest? doctest, documentation • Tests embedded in docstrings
• >>> add(2,3)\n5 — expected output
• python -m doctest module.py to run
• Good for documentation, not comprehensive testing
25 Test private methods — should you? Private, testing • Generally NO — test public interface instead
• Private methods are implementation details
• If complex enough to test separately, maybe extract to own class
• If needed: obj._ClassName__private()

Section 16: Performance & Optimization¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Profile a Python application? Profile, bottleneck • cProfile.run('main()') — function-level
• line_profiler — line-by-line
• py-spy — sampling profiler (no code changes)
• Profile first, optimize second
2 cProfile — reading output? cProfile, output • tottime — time in function (excluding sub-calls)
• cumtime — total time including sub-calls
• ncalls — number of calls
• Sort: cProfile.run('f()', sort='cumulative')
3 timeit — benchmarking? timeit, benchmark • timeit.timeit('expr', number=100000)
• CLI: python -m timeit 'expr'
• setup='import ...' for imports
• Multiple runs for reliability
4 Common Python bottlenecks? Bottleneck, slow • Nested loops over large data
• String concatenation with +=
• list membership testing (use set)
• Repeated function calls in tight loops
• Global variable access (slower than local)
5 Optimize loops? Loop, optimize • Move invariant code outside loop
• Use list comprehensions (30% faster)
• Local variable access faster than global
• Built-in functions (map, filter) in C
• Avoid range(len(x)) — use enumerate
6 join() faster than +=? join, concat, fast • += creates new string each iteration → O(n²)
• join() pre-allocates total size → O(n)
• 10x faster for large strings
• ''.join(parts) — always use in loops
7 set lookups vs list? set, lookup, O(1) • set: O(1) membership test (hash table)
• list: O(n) membership test (linear scan)
• x in large_set — instant
• x in large_list — slow
• Convert to set for repeated lookups
8 Generators to reduce memory? Generator, memory • Process items one at a time (O(1) memory)
• sum(x**2 for x in range(10**6)) — no list
• Pipeline: gen1 → gen2 → gen3 pattern
• Ideal for ETL, log processing
9 __slots__ for performance? slots, fast • 20-40% less memory per instance
• ~10% faster attribute access
• No per-instance __dict__
• Best for millions of instances
10 NumPy vectorized operations? NumPy, vectorize • C-level loops instead of Python loops
• np.array([1,2,3]) * 2 — vectorized
• 100x faster than Python loops for math
• Broadcasting eliminates explicit loops
11 Cython and ctypes? Cython, C, ctypes • Cython: Python-like syntax compiled to C
• ctypes: call C shared libraries from Python
• cffi — alternative to ctypes
• Used for hot paths needing C-level speed
12 Multiprocessing for CPU-bound? Multiprocessing, CPU • ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)
• Each process has its own GIL
• True parallelism on multi-core
• Overhead: process creation, serialization
13 GIL impact on performance? GIL, performance • CPU-bound threads: no speedup (single core)
• I/O-bound threads: full benefit (GIL released)
• Solution: multiprocessing, C extensions
• Python 3.13+ experimental free-threading
14 Cache expensive computations? Cache, memoize • @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=128) — function caching
• @functools.cache — unlimited cache (3.9+)
• Redis/memcached for distributed caching
• cachetools for TTL caches
15 Optimize database queries? Database, ORM • Use indexes on frequently queried columns
• Avoid N+1 queries (use select_related/joinedload)
• Batch operations instead of row-by-row
• Profile with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
16 Lazy loading? Lazy, deferred • Compute values only when needed
• @property for lazy attributes
• Generators for lazy sequences
• importlib.import_module() for lazy imports
17 Reduce startup time? Startup, import • Lazy imports (import inside function)
• Reduce import chain depth
• Use __all__ to limit star imports

18 Optimize pandas operations? pandas, optimize • Vectorized operations over apply()
• Appropriate dtypes (category, int32)
• chunksize for large CSVs
• Use query() method for filtering
19 PyPy vs CPython performance? PyPy, CPython • PyPy: JIT compiler, 5-10x faster for long-running code
• CPython: reference implementation, best library support
• PyPy: less memory for many objects
• PyPy: may not support all C extensions
20 __all__ and lazy imports? all, lazy import • __all__ limits import * (doesn't prevent import)
• Lazy imports: only import when first used
• Module __getattr__ for lazy attributes (PEP 562)
• Reduces import time for large packages

Section 17: Design Patterns & Best Practices¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Zen of Python — important principles? Zen, PEP 20 • Readability counts
• Explicit is better than implicit
• Simple is better than complex
• Errors should never pass silently
• import this to see all 19 aphorisms
2 Pythonic code — examples? Pythonic, idiomatic • for x in items: NOT for i in range(len(items))
• with open() as f: NOT manual open()/close()
• List comprehensions over map()/filter()
• if x: NOT if x == True:
3 SOLID principles in Python? SOLID, principles • Single Responsibility: one reason to change
• Open/Closed: extend, don't modify
• Liskov Substitution: subtypes must be substitutable
• Interface Segregation: specific interfaces
• Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions
4 Single Responsibility Principle? SRP, single • Class/function should have ONE reason to change
• UserRepository for DB, UserValidator for validation
• NOT User class doing everything
• Smaller, focused modules
5 Open/Closed Principle? OCP, extend • Open for extension, closed for modification
• Add new behavior via inheritance/composition
• Strategy pattern: swap algorithms without changing code
• Plugin architecture
6 Liskov Substitution Principle? LSP, subtype • Subclass must be usable wherever parent is used
• Don't violate parent's contract
• Square ≠ Rectangle (LSP violation)
• If it needs special handling, wrong abstraction
7 Dependency Injection in Python? DI, injection • Pass dependencies as parameters, don't hardcode
• def process(db: Database): — inject DB
• Constructor injection: __init__(self, db)
• No framework needed in Python
8 Common design patterns in Python? Patterns, common • Singleton (module-level), Factory, Observer
• Strategy (first-class functions), Iterator (built-in)
• Decorator (@ syntax), Template Method
• Many GoF patterns simplified by Python features
9 Iterator pattern — built into Python? Iterator, pattern • for loop IS the iterator pattern
• __iter__ / __next__ = iterator protocol
• Generators = easy iterators
• No separate Iterator class needed
10 First-class functions eliminate patterns? First-class, pattern • Strategy: just pass a function
• Command: function + closure
• Template Method: pass function for varying step
• Observer: list of callback functions
11 Repository pattern? Repository, data • Abstracts data access behind interface
• class UserRepo(Protocol): def get(id): ...
• Swap implementations: SQL, NoSQL, in-memory
• Decouples business logic from storage
12 Builder pattern? Builder, construct • Step-by-step object construction
• Method chaining: Query().select('*').where('x=1').limit(10)
• In Python: often just **kwargs or dataclass
• More useful for complex configuration
13 Adapter pattern? Adapter, interface • Converts one interface to another
• Wrap incompatible API in compatible wrapper
• class LegacyAdapter: def new_method(self): return self.old.old_method()
• Common in third-party integrations
14 YAGNI, DRY, KISS? YAGNI, DRY, KISS • YAGNI: You Aren't Gonna Need It — don't pre-build
• DRY: Don't Repeat Yourself — extract common code
• KISS: Keep It Simple — simplest solution wins
• Balance: don't over-engineer
15 Configuration management? Config, env • os.environ.get('KEY', 'default') — env vars
• .env files with python-dotenv
• dataclass for structured config
• Separate config per environment (dev/staging/prod)
16 Production project structure? Structure, project • src/mypackage/ layout
• tests/, docs/, scripts/
• pyproject.toml for metadata
• Makefile or just for common commands
17 Monolith vs well-structured modules? Monolith, module • Monolith: one big file, everything coupled
• Modular: small focused files, clear imports
• Start modular from day one
• Split when file exceeds ~300 lines
18 Dependency management: pip, pipenv, poetry? pip, poetry, deps • pip + requirements.txt — basic
• poetry — modern, lockfile, dependency resolution
• pipenv — pip + virtualenv (less popular now)
• uv — fastest, Rust-based (2024+)
19 Pre-commit hooks: black, ruff, mypy? pre-commit, linting • pre-commit — runs checks before git commit
• black — opinionated formatter
• ruff — ultra-fast linter (replaces flake8)
• mypy — static type checker
20 Decorator pattern (GoF) vs Python decorators? GoF, decorator • GoF: wraps object to add behavior at runtime
• Python @decorator: wraps function at definition
• Both add behavior without modifying original
• Python's is syntactic sugar for the GoF concept

Section 18: Python for Data & Real-World Scenarios¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Read CSV with millions of rows? CSV, large, pandas • pd.read_csv('f', chunksize=10000) — chunked
• csv.reader with lazy iteration
• polars — Rust-based, faster than pandas
• dask for out-of-memory DataFrames
2 pandas.read_csv() vs csv module? pandas, csv • pandas: DataFrame (analysis-ready), auto-types
• csv: raw lists/dicts, lightweight, no deps
• pandas: more memory, more features
• csv: for simple parsing or memory-constrained
3 Handle missing data in pandas? Missing, NaN, pandas • df.isnull(), df.dropna(), df.fillna(value)
• df.interpolate() — fill with interpolation
• pd.NA (nullable, 1.0+) vs np.nan
• Strategy depends on data context
4 NumPy arrays vs Python lists? NumPy, array, list • NumPy: fixed type, contiguous memory, vectorized
• List: mixed types, pointer array, Python loops
• NumPy: 10-100x faster for numerical ops
• NumPy: less memory per element
5 HTTP requests: requests vs httpx vs urllib? requests, httpx • urllib — built-in, verbose, low-level
• requests — simple, synchronous, most popular
• httpx — sync + async, HTTP/2 support
• Use httpx for new projects
6 Parse HTML/XML: BeautifulSoup, lxml? BeautifulSoup, scraping • BeautifulSoup — easy, forgiving HTML parser
• lxml — fast, XPath support
• soup.select('div.class') — CSS selectors
• lxml.etree for XML processing
7 Work with APIs: auth, pagination, rate limiting? API, auth, pagination • Auth: headers {'Authorization': 'Bearer token'}
• Pagination: loop with next_url or offset
• Rate limiting: time.sleep() or asyncio.Semaphore
• Use session for connection reuse
8 REST API: Flask vs FastAPI vs DRF? Flask, FastAPI, REST • Flask: minimal, flexible, synchronous
• FastAPI: async, auto-docs, type validation
• Django REST: full-featured, ORM integration
• FastAPI best for new Python APIs
9 WSGI vs ASGI? WSGI, ASGI • WSGI: synchronous protocol (Flask, Django)
• ASGI: async protocol (FastAPI, Starlette)
• ASGI needed for WebSockets, async views
• Servers: Gunicorn (WSGI), Uvicorn (ASGI)
10 Database connection: sqlite3, psycopg2, SQLAlchemy? Database, ORM • sqlite3 — built-in, file-based, single-user
• psycopg2 — PostgreSQL driver
• SQLAlchemy — ORM + Core, database-agnostic
• asyncpg for async PostgreSQL
11 ORM — pros and cons? ORM, SQLAlchemy • Pros: less SQL, database agnostic, Python objects
• Cons: performance overhead, complex queries harder
• N+1 query problem (fix with eager loading)
• Good for CRUD, raw SQL for complex analytics
12 Database migrations — Alembic? Alembic, migration • alembic revision --autogenerate -m 'msg'
• alembic upgrade head — apply migrations
• Tracks schema versions in database
• Pairs with SQLAlchemy models
13 Deploy Python app: Docker, Gunicorn? Deploy, Docker • Dockerfile with multi-stage build
• Gunicorn/Uvicorn as WSGI/ASGI server
• Docker Compose for local
• CMD ["gunicorn", "-w", "4", "app:app"]
14 Logging, monitoring, alerting in production? Logging, monitoring • Structured logging (JSON format)
• APM tools: Datadog, New Relic, Sentry
• Health check endpoints
• Centralized log aggregation (ELK, CloudWatch)
15 Environment-specific config? Config, environment • .env files per environment
• python-dotenv to load
• os.getenv('DB_URL', 'sqlite:///dev.db')
• pydantic-settings for validated config
16 celery for background tasks? Celery, async task • Distributed task queue with broker (Redis/RabbitMQ)
• @celery.task def send_email(to): …
• .delay(arg) to queue; .get() to wait
• Used for email, reports, heavy processing
17 Rate limiter in Python? Rate limiter, token • Token bucket algorithm: tokens -= 1; sleep if empty
• asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
• Redis-based for distributed systems
• Libraries: ratelimit, limits
18 Retry with exponential backoff? Retry, backoff • for i in range(n): try: …; break; except: sleep(2**i)
• tenacity library: @retry(wait=wait_exponential())
• Add jitter to prevent thundering herd
• Max retries to prevent infinite loops
19 Large file uploads in web app? Upload, large file • Stream in chunks (don't load all in memory)
• request.stream in Flask/FastAPI
• aiofiles for async file writes
• Progress: chunked transfer encoding
20 Design a URL shortener? URL shortener, design • Generate short code: hashlib.md5(url)[:6] or counter
• Store mapping: code → url in DB
• Redirect: 301 Moved Permanently
• Consider: collisions, analytics, expiry
21 Web scraper respecting robots.txt? Scraper, robots.txt • urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser() — check rules
• time.sleep(1) between requests
• Set User-Agent header
• Handle rate limits and errors gracefully
22 WebSockets in Python? WebSocket, real-time • websockets library (async)
• FastAPI: @app.websocket('/ws')
• Socket.IO for cross-platform real-time
• Use for: chat, live updates, streaming
23 pydantic vs dataclasses for validation? Pydantic, validation • Pydantic: runtime validation, coercion, JSON
• Dataclasses: no validation (just structure)
• pydantic.BaseModel auto-validates on creation
• Pydantic better for API input/output
24 typing.TypeGuard for type narrowing? TypeGuard, narrowing • def is_str_list(x) -> TypeGuard[list[str]]: (3.10+)
• Narrows type in if branch for type checker
• Runtime: just a regular bool function
• Helps mypy understand custom type checks
25 Key differences: Python 3.10-3.13? Python, versions • 3.10: match/case, union X \&#124; Y
• 3.11: ExceptionGroup, except*, 10-60% faster
• 3.12: f-string improvements, type statement
• 3.13: experimental free-threaded (no-GIL) mode

Section 19: Python Coding Interview Patterns¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Reverse a linked list? Linked list, reverse • Iterative: prev=None; while cur: nxt=cur.next; cur.next=prev; prev=cur; cur=nxt
• Recursive: reverse rest, point next to current
• Time O(n), Space O(1) iterative / O(n) recursive
2 Detect cycle in linked list? Cycle, Floyd • Floyd's algorithm: slow (1 step) + fast (2 steps)
• If they meet → cycle exists
• To find start: reset one to head, move both 1 step
• Time O(n), Space O(1)
3 Binary search? Binary search • lo, hi = 0, len(a)-1; while lo <= hi: mid = (lo+hi)//2
• if a[mid] == target: return mid
• elif a[mid] < target: lo = mid+1 else: hi = mid-1
• Time O(log n), Space O(1)
4 Two-sum problem? Two-sum, hash • Hash map: seen = {}; for i,n in enumerate(nums): comp = target-n; if comp in seen: return [seen[comp], i]; seen[n] = i
• Time O(n), Space O(n)
5 Longest substring without repeats? Sliding window, substring • Sliding window with set/dict
• Expand right, shrink left when duplicate found
• Track max length
• Time O(n), Space O(min(n, charset))
6 BFS and DFS? BFS, DFS, graph • BFS: queue, level-order, shortest path in unweighted
• DFS: stack/recursion, explore fully before backtrack
• BFS for shortest path; DFS for exhaustive search
• Both O(V + E)
7 Merge sort and quicksort? Merge sort, quicksort • Merge sort: divide, sort halves, merge — O(n log n) always, stable
• Quicksort: pivot, partition, recurse — O(n log n) avg, O(n²) worst
• Python's sorted() uses TimSort (hybrid)
8 Stable vs unstable sort? Stable, unstable, sort • Stable: equal elements keep original order
• Unstable: equal elements may be reordered
• Stable: merge sort, TimSort, insertion sort
• Unstable: quicksort, heapsort
9 Stack using two queues? Stack, queue • Push: enqueue to q1
• Pop: move all but last from q1 to q2, dequeue last, swap
• Or: on push, enqueue then rotate all previous to back
• Time: O(1) push, O(n) pop OR O(n) push, O(1) pop
10 Queue using two stacks? Queue, stack • Push stack + pop stack
• Enqueue: push to stack1
• Dequeue: if stack2 empty, transfer all from stack1; pop stack2
• Amortized O(1) per operation
11 Nth Fibonacci — memoization/DP? Fibonacci, DP • Naive recursion: O(2ⁿ) — too slow
• Memoization (@lru_cache): O(n) time, O(n) space
• Bottom-up DP: O(n) time, O(1) space
• a, b = b, a+b in loop
12 Binary search tree? BST, tree • Left child < parent < right child
• Insert/search/delete: O(h), h = height
• Balanced BST: O(log n) operations
• In-order traversal gives sorted order
13 Serialize/deserialize binary tree? Serialize, tree • BFS/DFS with None markers for empty nodes
• Serialize: '1,2,None,None,3'
• Deserialize: rebuild from string
• Use preorder for simpler implementation
14 Permutations and combinations? Permutations, backtrack • itertools.permutations(items, r) — ordered arrangements
• itertools.combinations(items, r) — unordered selections
• Backtracking: swap/include-exclude pattern
• Permutations: n!, Combinations: n!/(r!(n-r)!)
15 Sliding window technique? Sliding window • Fixed window: sum of k elements (add right, subtract left)
• Variable window: expand right, shrink left by condition
• Use for: subarray problems, substring problems
• Time O(n), Space O(1) usually
16 Merge two sorted lists? Merge, sorted • Two pointers, compare heads, advance smaller
• while i < len(a) and j < len(b): if a[i] <= b[j]: …
• Append remaining elements
• Time O(n+m), Space O(n+m)
17 Kth largest element? Kth largest, heap • heapq.nlargest(k, nums)[-1] — O(n log k)
• Min-heap of size k: push then pop if > k
• Quickselect: O(n) average, O(n²) worst
• sorted(nums)[-k] — O(n log n)
18 Hash map from scratch? Hash map, implement • Array of buckets, hash function
• hash(key) % size → bucket index
• Chaining: linked list per bucket
• Resize when load factor > 0.75
19 Balanced parentheses? Parentheses, stack • Stack: push on ({[, pop and match on )}]
• If mismatch or stack not empty → invalid
• Handle all 3 types: (), {}, []
• Time O(n), Space O(n)
20 Topological sort? Topological, DAG • Order vertices so every edge u→v has u before v
• Only for DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs)
• Kahn's (BFS with in-degree) or DFS post-order
• Used for: build order, prerequisites
21 Coin change — dynamic programming? Coin change, DP • dp[i] = min coins for amount i
• dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin] + 1) for each coin
• Bottom-up: fill dp table 0 to amount
• Time O(amount × coins), Space O(amount)
22 Longest common subsequence? LCS, DP • 2D DP: dp[i][j] = LCS of s1[:i] and s2[:j]
• If match: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1
• Else: max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])
• Time O(m×n), Space O(m×n) or O(n) optimized
23 Trie for autocomplete? Trie, autocomplete • Insert: traverse/create nodes per char, mark end
• Search prefix: traverse nodes to prefix end
• Autocomplete: DFS from prefix node to find all words
• Time O(m) per operation (m = word length)
24 heapq for median finding? Median, two heaps • Two heaps: max-heap (left) + min-heap (right)
• Balance: sizes differ by at most 1
• Median: top of larger heap (or average of both)
• Insert: O(log n), Find median: O(1)
25 Two-pointer technique? Two pointer, sorted • Start/end pointers moving inward (sorted array)
• Fast/slow pointers (linked list cycle)
• Used for: pair sum, container with most water
• Time O(n), Space O(1)
26 Graph using adjacency list? Graph, adjacency • graph = defaultdict(list); graph[u].append(v)
• Undirected: add both u→v and v→u
• Weighted: graph[u].append((v, weight))
• Space O(V + E)
27 Shortest path in unweighted graph? Shortest path, BFS • BFS from source — first visit is shortest
• Track distance: dist[v] = dist[u] + 1
• Reconstruct path: track parent of each node
• Time O(V + E)
28 Detect duplicates O(n) time O(1) space? Duplicates, Floyd • If values in range [1, n]: use Floyd's cycle detection
• Or use sign-marking: nums[abs(n)-1] *= -1
• With extra space: set() is O(n) time O(n) space
• Trade-offs depend on constraints
29 Rotate matrix 90 degrees? Matrix, rotate • Transpose then reverse each row
• matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i] = matrix[j][i], matrix[i][j]
• Then reverse: row.reverse()
• In-place, Time O(n²), Space O(1)
30 LRU cache with OrderedDict? LRU, OrderedDict • class LRU(OrderedDict): def __getitem__(self, k): self.move_to_end(k); return super().__getitem__(k)
• On insert: if over capacity self.popitem(last=False)
• All operations O(1)
• Or use @functools.lru_cache
